name: Kovalam Reef (Lighthouse Beach, Kerala, India)

confidence.reason: Only one oblique, unscaled photo shows the structure, and the scale (camera height) is not fixed by the picture: footprint 550-1,700 m2 for camera heights 30-80 m. The position is tied to the 2011 satellite swash line (+-15 m) and the long-shore size agrees with the 65 m of a secondary table, but the cross-shore size does not (41 vs 85 m).
factors: single oblique photo, no scale bar, no ground control survey
camera height free: rms 2.2-2.8 px for H 30-80 m
swash line used for the fit differs in date from the photo (2011-02 satellite vs 2010-11 aerial)
left (seaward) end of the strips fades into haze
no as-built drawing or survey found; reef later deflated and sank (not drawn)

design_version.drawn: As-built reef of ASR Ltd, completed late Feb 2010 (4,000 m3 per Mead & Borrero 2011; card 4,800 m3), as seen in the ASR aerial taken between completion and March 2011.
design_version.why_this_one: It is the only built version; the 2005 Kerala Tourism proposal (500 m long, 200 m offshore, Eve's Beach) was never built. The aerial shows it intact, before the 2010-2011 deflation reported by Raised Water Research.

versions_info: Three outlines of the same sand-container strips, all traced on the ASR aerial photo (taken between completion in Feb 2010 and March 2011) and placed on the 2011-02-28 satellite frame through a fitted camera. They differ only in the assumed camera height (35, 60, 80 m), which the photo cannot fix, so they show the scale uncertainty. Default 60 m: it reproduces the 90 m offshore distance of the WRL review table with a normal wide-angle lens. No survey or design drawing of the built reef was found.

page_status.why: Only one oblique, unscaled photo shows the structure and the photo cannot fix the scale: the traced strips cover 546 to 1,681 m2 depending on the assumed camera height (35, 60, 80 m shown as versions). No survey, plan or vertical image exists, so the reef's true size and place are unknown.

2011-02-28 swash line represents the beach at the time of the photo (2010-11)
Strips plus whitewater patch = the reef; faint streaks and haze tip excluded or guessed
